correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the normalized masses q^j(A+Bj) by telescoping the survival function (q=e^(−σ), a=σ/(1+σ³), A=1−q−qa>0, B=(1−q)a>0). Their log-concavity difference is q^(2j)B². The PGF is A(1+cz)/(1−qz)² with c/q=B/A−1>−1, giving log coefficients (2q^n+(−1)^(n+1)c^n)/n. For necessity, if a positive-at-zero PGF has convolution roots of every order N, each nonconstant coefficient of its normalized Nth root is ν_n/N+O(N^(−2)) at fixed n and must be nonnegative. For c≤q all ν_n here are positive and summable, and normalization yields the explicit compound-Poisson PGF including equality; for c>q sufficiently high even coefficients are negative. Algebra gives the criterion a≤2 tanh(σ/2). Checked the all-positive series for D(x) starting at degree six, and hence the strict decrease from infinity to zero of [(σ/2)coth(σ/2)−1]/σ³. Independently verified the exact numeric bounds using rational arithmetic: for each of the two rational endpoints and s=1/20 bound e^s between its degree-24 Taylor sum L and U=L+2s^25/25!, valid since all omitted successive term ratios are <1/2. For G(s,E)=(2−a(s))(E−1)−2a(s), G(left,U)<0<G(right,L). At s=1/20 the denominator E−1−a is positive on [L,U]; t(E)=a(E−1)/(E−1−a)−1 decreases, and exact comparisons give t(U)>1 and t(L)^102<2<t(U)^104. This certifies the specific obstruction at degree 104 without using the supplied script. Minor diagnostic reporting issue: check_exact.py prints 400 auxiliary compound-Poisson coefficient checks, but its conditional skips the fourth example (c/q=4/3), so that loop checks 300 coefficients; this does not affect any claimed theorem, interval or negative coefficient. The review is only of ordinary additive convolution on nonnegative integers, not thinning.

value.rationale: The parameter curve is fixed by a published count model rather than chosen to manufacture a root. Despite strict log-concavity throughout the model, the rate determines precisely when an ordinary compound-Poisson representation is possible. Knowing the exact cutoff and jump intensities is useful for that interpretation and simulation, and the explicit high-degree failure demonstrates why checking some low logarithmic coefficients cannot decide the model's divisibility. Value does not depend on whether the witness contradicts the published Das theorem as worded.
